topic: Verify DeepSeek v4.1-flash weights before you run them
title: Verify your DeepSeek v4.1-flash weights
description: Prime Intellect served substituted DeepSeek v4.1-flash weights for over two days and no benchmark noticed. Here is how to pin the revision and hash your GGUF shards before you load them. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: Prime Intellect served the wrong weights for over two days.
Ninety-eight refusals out of a hundred became one.
Same endpoint name. Different weights inside.
Your model download has no tamper-evident seal. It has one better thing.
Two hundred thirty-three gigabytes, and nothing checks them.
The benchmark passed. The weights were fake.
Wrong weights. Two days. Nobody benchmarked it.
It still aced every test. It was not the model.
Your GGUF shards trust the name on the folder.
Hash it before you load it.
narration_full: Prime Intellect served the wrong weights for over two days. Same endpoint, different DeepSeek weights answering you. Capability scores never moved. On JailbreakBench, a refusal test, ninety-eight of one hundred refusals became one. Scores grade answers, not origins. Unsloth's smallest one-bit pack is a GGUF your runner loads: two hundred thirty-three gigabytes of weights, never hashed. Same restaurant sign, different kitchen; diners can peek, clients cannot, so check files. Tonight, pin the revision, the full commit hash. Fetch the manifest, the list of expected fingerprints. No hash, no load. A match proves Hugging Face's bits arrived, never that they deserved trust. Verify every pull before you load it.

analogy.vehicle: A restaurant that keeps the sign but swaps the kitchen.
analogy.mapping: Prime Intellect's endpoint kept its name, chat template and tokenizer while different weights answered, so every client vouched for the sign instead of the kitchen.
analogy.limit: A diner can walk in and inspect the kitchen; an API client cannot inspect weights mid-conversation, which is why the check has to happen on the files before loading.

As 'different DeepSeek weights answering you' lands, the second block's model tag flickers once and settles on 'abliterated-copy' in amber. Cursor blinks at the bottom. Everything holds a beat before the flicker; only the tag and the cursor ever move. Motion onset: the second reply block's header flashes amber at 0.4 s; cursor blinks 530 ms.

Right pane shows 'JailbreakBench refusals' with a counter reading '98/100'. On 'became one' the counter hard-cuts to '1/100' in red and the right pane border tints red. On 'not origins' the left pane dims slightly. Hard cuts only, no dissolve, one motion at a time.

On 'check files' the giant number drops to a corner and the cursor returns to the prompt. Entrances are typewriter or fade only.

On 'fetch the manifest' a 'SHA256SUMS' file row fades in beside it. On 'Check before loading' the rows 'sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS' and 'hf cache verify' type in sequence, each returning a green 'OK'. One typing cursor at a time; rows snap in place, nothing slides from an edge.

On the payoff, a final prompt line rises-in-place: 'verify every pull', and the cursor holds steady after it. Nothing else moves; the frame ends on that line.
